newsitem.title: USA: Gaylord Container low prices mean Q3 loss.
newsitem.headline: Gaylord Container low prices mean Q3 loss.

text.p: Gaylord Container Corp said Wednesday lower product pricing and a charge from retiring debt resulted in a net loss in its third quarter.

"Lower average net selling prices accounted for essentially all of the decline in operating earnings," said chairman and chief executive officer Marvin A. Pomerantz, in a statement accompanying its third quarter results.

The company reported a net loss of $27.6 million ($0.53 per share) for the third quarter of fiscal 1997 ended June 30, 1997, which included an extraordinary loss of $7.7 million, or $0.15 per share, on the early retirement of debt.
This compares to net income of $0.1 million ($0.00 per share) in the third quarter of fiscal 1996.
Net sales declined 16 percent to $189.4 million in the third quarter of fiscal 1997 compared to $225.5 million in the year-earlier period.
The company reported an operating loss of $11.2 million in the third quarter of fiscal 1997 compared to operating earnings of $18.9 million in the year-ago third quarter.
Despite increased mill production, Gaylord said its inventories declined by more than 14,000 tons (12 percent) versus March 1997 levels.
Corrugated shipments totaled 3.5 billion square feet in the third quarter of fiscal 1997, up approximately three percent, from 3.4 billion square feet in the year-ago quarter.

Gaylord said it is currently implementing a linerboard price increase of $40 per ton effective with orders entered for shipment on or after July 1, 1997 and has announced a box price increase of 12 percent effective on July 28, 1997.
It said the increases are in line with recent industry statistics indicating strong demand in both the U.S. corrugated container market and in the export market.

"As we look to the future, we see a strong U.S. economy and a strengthening global economy, suggesting increased demand for packaging papers around the world for some time to come. In addition to strong demand, we see limited supply additions...Given our view of continuing strong demand and limited new supply, we remain optimistic about the future of our business and our company," it said.
Gaylord Container Corp is a national manufacturer and distributor of corrugated containers and sheets, containerboard, unbleached kraft paper and multiwall bags.
